passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Good morning. My name is Sarah, and I will be your conference operator today. I would like to welcome everyone to the Third Quarter SLB Earnings Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a Q&A session. To ask a question, press 1 on your telephone keypad. You may remove yourself from the queue by pressing 1 again. As a reminder, this call is being recorded. I will now turn the call over to James R. McDonald, Senior Vice President of Investor Relations and Industry Affairs. Please go ahead.

passages.heading: James R. McDonald, Senior Vice President of Investor Relations and Industry Affairs
passages.text: James R. McDonald, Senior Vice President of Investor Relations and Industry Affairs: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, and welcome to the SLB Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Today's call is being hosted from New York City following our board meeting held earlier this week. Joining us on the call are Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer, and Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer. Before we begin, I would like to remind all participants that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These matters involve risks and uncertainties that could cause our results to differ materially from those projected in these statements. For more information, please refer to our latest 10-K filing and other SEC filings, which can be found on our website. Our comments today also include non-GAAP financial measures. Additional details and reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures can be found in our third quarter earnings press release, which is on our website. With that, I will turn the call over to Olivier.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Thank you, James. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for joining us. Today, I will begin with our third quarter performance. I will then discuss the evolving macro environment and the fundamentals supporting our outlook as we approach 2027. Finally, I will share our expectations for the fourth quarter. Stephane will then provide additional details on our financial results, and after that, we will open the line for your questions. Let's begin. The third quarter was marked by broad-based sequential revenue growth across each of our geographic areas and core divisions, with pretax segment operating margins expanding across all four divisions. This was driven by the gradual recovery in the Middle East, solid growth in North America, and continued momentum across the international offshore basins, including Latin America, Europe and Africa, and Asia. Within the core divisions, Production Systems led the way, supported by higher 3D revenue and strong sales of production chemicals and artificial lift in North America and the Middle East. Notably, ChampionX delivered its highest quarterly revenue since the acquisition, with margins expanding sequentially for the fourth consecutive quarter. Well Construction growth was driven by double-digit increases across Argentina, Guyana, Brazil, and U.S. land, along with the seasonal recovery in Canada, complemented by strong offshore drilling in Asia. Sequential growth was also driven by

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: higher drilling activity and frac and cementing in the Middle East. While the near-term pace of recovery in the Middle East remains uncertain, the longer-term outlook continues to strengthen. This is reflected by Saudi Aramco's recent award of four integrated well construction contracts to SLB, covering more than 450 wells over an initial three-year term. These multiyear awards significantly improve our revenue visibility and expand our participation in development activity across the Kingdom. By bringing together our digital training workflows, automated technologies, and integrated well construction portfolio, we can deliver this work effectively. Reservoir Performance also delivered strong sequential growth, led by increased stimulation and intervention activity, alongside an uptick in evaluation. This demonstrates that customers are investing both in restoration and production optimization of existing assets, and in the evaluation of reservoirs to support new development. Results this quarter continue to demonstrate the benefits of our strategic focus on production recovery. Our production business, encompassing all of Production Systems and some of the offerings in Reservoir Performance, now represents more than 50% of our portfolio. We have a leading position across every major basin and an advanced mix of short- and long-cycle activity, including exposure to resilient OpEx spend. This provides a durable foundation with greater revenue visibility and returns on

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: performance across market cycles. Taken together, growth across all core divisions reflects the characteristics of an inflecting upcycle, with broad expansion of activity across exploration, development, and intervention as operators ramp up efforts to restore production and bring new capacity online. In Digital, third quarter revenue was steady sequentially, and margins remained strong, despite digital exploration sales declining following exceptional sales in the second quarter. Customers continue to recognize the benefits of AI and digital operations, and we delivered more than 750,000 feet of automated drilling this quarter, an increase of nearly 50% year on year. Additionally, the Helix predictive analytics, intelligent real-time monitoring, and advisory system is now monitoring more than 20% of active international rigs, representing year-on-year growth of more than 60%. As you can see, adoption continues to accelerate, and we are very pleased with the progress of our Digital business. Digital has grown 11% year to date, and we have clear visibility into higher sales in the fourth quarter. As a result, we anticipate finishing the year with double-digit year-on-year growth and adjusted EBITDA margins above 35%. Finally, Data Center Solutions continued its strong growth trajectory, supported by the progression of existing projects and geographic expansion into Asia. During the quarter, we continued to invest in facilities and talent to expand our execution capacity,

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: including a new manufacturing center in Canada to support the Meta data center project. These investments are essential to meet surging customer demand. Upon closing of our previously announced acquisition of Kelvion, the Kelvion portfolio will also benefit greatly from this momentum and will accelerate our ambition to become a leading industrial partner in future AI infrastructure. In summary, I am extremely proud of our third quarter performance, and I want to thank the entire SLB team for delivering these results. Their focus on execution, innovation, and customer centricity continues to make the difference. Let me now turn to the macro environment and the fundamentals supporting our outlook as we approach 2027. Ongoing disruptions continue to reinforce the importance of energy security and the need for reliable, geographically diverse sources of supply. At the same time, the industry continues to face the structural challenge of offsetting natural decline and replacing reserves following several years of limited exploration. Collectively, these conditions are supporting a broader and increasingly diversified international opportunity. In the near term, this will support production intervention and other short-cycle activity. Longer term, it is providing a strong foundation for the progression of offshore developments, renewed exploration, and new areas of investment emerging across several markets. Let me briefly discuss how these long-cycle dynamics are evolving.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Deepwater represents one of the industry's most advantageous sources of new supply, combining attractive project economics, material resource developments, and long-duration production. We continue to see this opportunity broaden across Latin America, Africa, the Eastern Mediterranean, and Asia. Third-party FIDs are expected to increase more than 30% year on year in 2026, with many projects advancing from function into execution. For SLB, this momentum is reflected in the continued flow of OneSubsea awards, further strengthening our backlog and increasing visibility into 2027 and beyond. One example is our recent award in Mozambique, where OneSubsea was selected to deliver subsea production systems for the first phase of the deepwater Rovuma energy development. This project will contribute to an important new source of global gas supply and further demonstrate the progression of large, long-cycle deepwater developments into execution. In addition, fundamentals for exploration are improving as operators seek to replace reserves and diversify supply following several years of restrained investment. We see this materializing through new licensing activity in Brazil, the Eastern Mediterranean, and West Africa; growing interest in frontier basins such as Namibia; and preparations for future campaigns across deepwater markets, including Guyana and Suriname. As exploration assumes a greater role in our customer portfolio, SLB's leading position across exploration data, subsurface

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: modeling, and evaluation technologies positions us to capture this growing opportunity. So far this year, SLB has participated in the evaluation of approximately 80% of completed high-impact exploration wells globally, many of which are concentrated in frontier and deepwater basins. Beyond deepwater and exploration, international markets are offering new pathways for growth, with opportunities broadening across conventional and unconventional resources in the Middle East, as well as key emerging markets. In this context, Venezuela represents a particularly significant growth driver for SLB. Following more than a decade of limited investment, activity in the country is accelerating, led by international oil companies. For SLB, this is already translating to revenue growth. Our revenue in Venezuela is on track to more than double this year, with strong momentum among U.S. and European E&Ps supporting the potential for multifold growth in 2027. At the same time, major U.S. shale operators are expanding internationally, entering new countries and partnering with NOCs. This trend further broadens the addressable market, particularly in exploration and deepwater development across Africa, Latin America, and Asia, as well as unconventional resources in the Middle East. Looking across these dynamics—long-cycle offshore developments, renewed exploration, digital adoption, and U.S. operators expanding globally—all confirm a durable multiyear international investment cycle with clear

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: visibility into 2027 and beyond. With a market-leading position across our core divisions, an established leadership position in global production, differentiated digital capabilities, and an unmatched global footprint, SLB is uniquely positioned to capture this upside. Now let me conclude with our expectations for the fourth quarter and our first view of the 2027 market outlook. Over the past several weeks, the Middle East has continued to experience heightened tensions. Given the ongoing uncertainty, our fourth quarter outlook assumes Middle East revenue remains flat sequentially at approximately $1.9 billion, representing about 83% of the revenue generated in the fourth quarter of 2025. Based on this assumption, and supported by continued deepwater momentum as well as the typical year-end strength in Digital and product sales, we expect overall fourth quarter revenue to reach approximately $10 billion, representing an increase of 5% to 7% sequentially. As a result, when excluding the Middle East, global fourth quarter revenue is expected to grow in the high single digits year on year. We also expect adjusted EBITDA margins to expand 100 to 150 basis points. At the division level, we anticipate combined revenue from the core divisions to increase sequentially by low single digits, led by high single-digit growth in Production Systems, with Well Construction and Reservoir Performance essentially flat. In Digital, revenue is expected to increase in line with fourth quarter

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: historical trends, led by a significant uptick in typical year-end digital exploration sales. This outlook provides clear evidence that the next phase of the upcycle is underway. While near-term performance is dependent on geopolitical developments, a resolution of regional disruption in the Middle East could unlock deferred activity and serve as a powerful catalyst for accelerated growth in 2027. Looking ahead to 2027, assuming Middle East activity remains at second half 2026 levels and that the conflict does not materially escalate, we expect global OFS market activity to grow in the mid-single digits, with normalization of activity in the Middle East providing further upside. Against this backdrop, we expect our core divisions to visibly outperform the market, reflecting our differentiated exposure to the strongest areas of activity, including long-cycle offshore developments, renewed exploration activity, production recovery investments, and the activation of Venezuela. Beyond the core, we expect Digital to continue its established growth trajectory, while our Data Center Solutions business will continue to accelerate as a meaningful growth engine for the company. I will now turn the call over to Stephane to discuss our financial results in more detail.

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer: Thank you, Olivier, and good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Third quarter earnings per share, excluding charges and credits, was $0.64. This represents an increase of $0.09 sequentially and a decrease of $0.05 compared with the third quarter of last year. During the quarter, we recorded $0.03 of merger and integration charges related to the ChampionX transaction, as well as a $0.12, or $187 million, noncash pension settlement charge. This was the result of offering a lump-sum payment to certain former employees in one of our pension plans. This transaction, which was funded directly by assets of the plan, allowed us to derisk our largest pension plan by reducing both our pension obligations and plan assets by almost $900 million. This will help us lower potential volatility as well as manage future pension costs. Importantly, the plan remains very well funded. Overall, our third quarter revenue of $9.45 billion increased 5% sequentially. This performance was driven by the Middle East, growth in North America, and strong international deepwater activity, including upside in OneSubsea. In the Middle East, we experienced a gradual recovery, as third quarter revenue of $1.9 billion increased 13% from the previous quarter. Sequentially, our pretax segment operating margin increased 104 basis points, with margin expansion across all four divisions. Companywide adjusted EBITDA margin for the third quarter was 21.9%, representing a

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: sequential increase of 71 basis points. Let me now go through the third quarter results for each division. Third quarter Digital revenue of $693 million was essentially flat sequentially, as strong platform and application sales and higher revenue from digital operations and professional services were offset by lower digital exploration revenue following a very strong second quarter. Digital pretax operating margin of 28% increased 27 basis points, as improved profitability in digital operations and platforms and applications more than offset the effects of lower sales of exploration data licenses and transfer fees. We expect digital exploration revenue to increase significantly in the fourth quarter, which will result in strong year-on-year growth for the Digital division and adjusted EBITDA margin above 35% for the full year. Reservoir Performance revenue of $1.6 billion increased 5% sequentially, while pretax operating margin of 16.3% increased 140 basis points. These increases were primarily driven by the gradual recovery in the Middle East. Well Construction revenue of $2.9 billion increased 5% sequentially, primarily driven by higher drilling activity in the Middle East. Pretax operating margin of 16.4% improved 122 basis points, mostly due to the Middle East activity rebound. Production Systems revenue of $4 billion increased 6% sequentially, driven by the recovery of Middle East activity, increased sales in North America, and strong OneSubsea activity. OneSubsea

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: also recorded a steady flow of new contract awards, increasing backlog and further enhancing subsea revenue visibility into 2027. Production Systems pretax operating margin of 16.1% increased 60 basis points, with broad-based growth in OneSubsea, artificial lift, completions, and production chemicals. Notably, the acquired ChampionX businesses delivered their highest quarterly revenue and margin since joining SLB. Finally, in the All Other category, revenue increased 8% sequentially, driven by strong growth in Data Center Solutions, while pretax operating income decreased slightly as a result of ramp-up costs associated with new data center projects. With regard to our previously announced agreement to acquire Kelvion, things are progressing quite well. A dedicated integration team has been put in place and has kicked off its various work streams. We are in the process of making all necessary filings in the relevant jurisdictions. We are very excited about the opportunities that this transaction will bring, and we remain on track for closing in the first half of 2027. Now turning to our liquidity. We ended the quarter with net debt of $9.2 billion, the same level as the first quarter of last year. We generated $1.5 billion of cash flow from operations and $828 million of free cash flow. Looking ahead, consistent with our historical pattern, we expect a meaningful step-up in free cash flow in the fourth quarter, supported by lower inventory following year-end product sales

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: and higher customer collections. The magnitude of the sequential increase in free cash flow will largely depend on the timing of collections in certain countries. Capital investments, inclusive of CapEx and investments in APS projects and exploration data, were $682 million in the third quarter. For the full year, we still expect capital investments to be approximately $2.5 billion. During the quarter, we repurchased $656 million of our stock and are on track to repurchase approximately $2.4 billion for the full year, in line with 2025 levels. This will bring our total returns to shareholders for 2026 slightly above $4 billion, in line with the commitment we made earlier this year. I will now turn the call back to Olivier.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Thank you, Stephane. I believe, Sarah, that we are ready to take questions.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the Q&A session. Your first question comes from the line of James West with Melius Research. Your line is open.

passages.heading: James West, Analyst
passages.text: James West, Analyst: Hey. Good morning, Olivier and Stephane. Olivier, I think in your prepared remarks, it seems like almost every part of your business, whether product line or region, excluding the Middle East, of course, which still has uncertainty, is inflecting higher. I am curious if you could parse that out a little further and let us know which areas, products, product lines, or service lines you think will grow faster than others.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Thank you, James. We believe indeed that the cycle has started, and I think it has characteristics that are favorable to our footprint and to the composition of our business lines. We are seeing a combination of a deepwater and exploration rebound, which is long cycle. We see investment flowing to production recovery to improve production on existing assets. And we see the development of new geographic areas that are attracting investment, such as Venezuela and Argentina. All of this is happening without the catalyst of a resolution in the Middle East, which would add growth. So I believe that we are set for all divisions and all basins to benefit from growth in 2027 and beyond. We believe, again, that it goes from Digital to production recovery, from deepwater to unconventional, with exploration being an uptick that will match very well our footprint and our portfolio of technology. So, yes, it is broadly an inflection characteristic of a long-duration upcycle.

passages.heading: James West, Analyst
passages.text: James West, Analyst: Great. That is very helpful. On the exploration side, I recently spoke to a group of explorationists and spent some time with the heads of many of the major oil companies, and then, of course, with one of your senior people as well. Capital is definitely flowing there. For the first time in maybe a decade, they were happy about capital. Where are you seeing the most exciting activity in exploration at this point?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: I think we see several things. What is very good in this exploration cycle is that it is a mix of infrastructure-led exploration in very well-known natural basins, where pockets of oil or gas can be unlocked and connected to, with opportunities for sizable development. I think that relates to the mature basins of West Africa, as well as the North Sea on both sides of the sector, and then obviously the Gulf of Mexico. There are also a lot of frontier basins expanding. I think this is partly across the Americas and Brazil. The Pelotas Basin is attracting a lot of attention, as is the Atlantic margin on the Equatorial Margin, along with continued investment in Suriname and Guyana. Those are clearly in the spotlight. The same is true in Namibia and farther in the Namib Basin in Angola, as another part of Africa, and in the Eastern Mediterranean. Then I could keep going east to India and Indonesia, which have attracted a lot of investment due to gas reserves and potential there. Large discoveries have been made and are now entering subsea development going forward. All of this combines to make an exciting cycle for exploration. I think the combination of energy security as a heightened priority, depleting reserves, and the pressure of declining production is adding to and fueling this investment in exploration.

passages.heading: James West, Analyst
passages.text: James West, Analyst: Great. Thanks, Olivier.

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer: Thank you, James.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Your next question comes from Scott Gruber with Citigroup. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Scott Gruber, Analyst
passages.text: Scott Gruber, Analyst: Thanks, and good morning, Olivier and Stephane. You outlined a number of growth drivers into 2027, but I am curious because this is a question we often get from investors. If we see resolution in the Middle East in the not-too-distant future and crude moderates back to $65 or $70, similar to what we saw back in June, how resilient do you think the growth drivers would prove to be? Obviously, the Middle East would improve. But do you see much risk to the mid-single-digit growth outlook, excluding the Middle East, at more midcycle crude prices, or would the secular elements at play here sustain a healthy growth rate?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Scott, I believe we should keep in mind that a lot of barrels have been lost as a result of this crisis. There has been a lot of pull on reserves, commercial inventories, and strategic inventories. I think it is clear that additional barrels need to be brought into supply through activity in the future. Additionally, the realization that energy security is vital to the future of economic growth is also adding to the diversity of supply. This reinforces the conditions I commented on earlier regarding exploration. These conditions are not here for one year or six months. The upcycle has strong legs, both on the long-cycle side, including exploration and deepwater, and on the short-cycle side, including production recovery activity that is materializing across the board and is very well illustrated in the growth we are enjoying. That will be the base for the 2027 outlook. We believe the market is set for mid-single-digit global activity growth, assuming the Middle East is flat compared with 2026. This means that we are set to visibly outperform this, and the Middle East catalyst will become an additional catalyst upon a peace deal going forward.

passages.heading: Scott Gruber, Analyst
passages.text: Scott Gruber, Analyst: I appreciate that. I wanted to turn to Venezuela. The opportunity here certainly appears to be materializing more quickly than anyone anticipated initially. Can you provide more color on what you are seeing in the market? You mentioned that Venezuela could double this year, with multifold growth in 2027. How large could Venezuela become for SLB in two to three years? I know you said around a billion dollars at the peak back then. I am curious, at a high level, where you think the market could grow to in the next two to three years.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: We remain very excited about Venezuela. Every time we look into it, I think we realize that activity is set to increase further, and we are getting several catalysts for this. First and foremost, in lockstep with our customer, with whom we have been working for the last two years, we are seeing activity increase currently and in the near future. They have announced further increases in CapEx in the region, so we will be fully part of bringing this upside. Additionally, several of our international operators have made commitments and reached agreements in the country. We have benefited from this by signing contracts, and we have already started execution on another large contract this quarter. So we expect this to continue going forward. How big can it become? I think we have mentioned that the potential is for multifold growth next year, and we see this trajectory certainly continuing going forward. We have mentioned before the historical level of $1 billion of revenue in the long term. We do not see why that could not be a target or an ambition going forward. We are well prepared. We are adding resources and equipment, and gaining trust because we have a unique capacity on the ground and the ability to deliver.

passages.heading: Scott Gruber, Analyst
passages.text: Scott Gruber, Analyst: Well, great. I appreciate the color. Thank you.

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer: Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Your next question comes from Saurabh Pant with Bank of America. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Saurabh Pant, Analyst
passages.text: Saurabh Pant, Analyst: Hi. Good morning, Olivier and Stephane. Olivier, maybe I want to dig into the Middle East topic a little bit. We saw you deliver a strong 13% increase in Middle East revenue, despite some late-quarter disruption, right? That implies you were running ahead of expectations before the disruption hit. Can you share more color on the disruption and whether these disruptions are continuing right now? And what was driving the stronger-than-anticipated recovery before the disruptions hit? I know you talked about some contracts and leading those integrated drilling contracts. Maybe give us some color on all of that.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Yes. First, I think several countries participated in the pickup of activity in the third quarter as the security situation started to ease in several countries. I think this included the UAE and Kuwait, and to a lesser extent Qatar and Saudi Arabia. The beginning of the quarter clearly had an increase in activity, and this was reflected in some of the intervention, stimulation, and drilling activity across the region. Iraq, by contrast, was not necessarily getting the same uplift in activity, while Oman was steady. That situation turned out to be slightly ahead of expectations at the run rate as of midquarter. At the end of the quarter, some activity adjustments were made, and I think this was fairly precise. I do not want to revisit the specifics. We see things stabilizing, though. Hence, our expectation is that the fourth quarter will be at the current level of disruption, without further escalation of the conflict into a worst-case scenario. We are seeing that the fourth quarter will be in line with the third quarter, and that is our assumption. This is also the hypothesis we have used for our guidance on the 2027 market outlook. Regarding the integrated contracts, we are very pleased with these awards, which touch both gas and oil assets. This activity is definitely going forward, and we are mobilizing in the fourth quarter. It will come to full capacity in 2027. This is not affected; these are committed contracts for which we

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: are indeed getting resources and increased activity going forward.

passages.heading: Saurabh Pant, Analyst
passages.text: Saurabh Pant, Analyst: Got it. Thank you. That is very useful color, Olivier. For my follow-up, I will stick to the Middle East and focus on margins. I know there are lots of crosscurrents and a lot of uncertainty, but given everything we have heard about disruptions and cost inflation, and then some pricing pressure on larger tenders, how should we think about where margins can go in 2027? More broadly, if revenue in the Middle East normalizes to, say, the pre-conflict level, can margins normalize to that level immediately, or would it take more time because of everything going on with pricing and costs?

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer: Saurabh, Stephane here. You are using the Middle East as a swing factor for margins, and it is clearly a significant dilutive effect this year. Looking at the year-on-year performance, as we have indicated earlier, we have intentionally decided to address only partially the resources in the Middle East so as not to hamper our capacity to address the activity rebound. We are keeping some resources in place. When the conflict is resolved and activity rebounds, we will have very strong operating leverage, with very few additional costs to bring in. As a result, that will increase margins. Now, the overall level of company margins will not be driven only by the Middle East. We will likely have fewer inflation effects going into 2027 because those are already kind of baked in, if you will. We also hope that pricing pressure we have experienced in some of our core divisions will abate; that pressure is also baked into current margins. But then you have the mix of divisions. Digital is a booster, obviously, on margins. Data Center Solutions, as it grows very fast, is not accretive to the overall SLB margin, as you know. It is a big equation, and we are not going to give you the answer today. We will provide more color on our 2027 margins in January. But overall, yes, the Middle East will be a catalyst for margin expansion for SLB.

passages.heading: Saurabh Pant, Analyst
passages.text: Saurabh Pant, Analyst: Thanks, Stephane. That equation is on us to solve in the interim. Thank you.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Thanks for considering all the moving pieces.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Your next question comes from Arun Jayaram with JPMorgan. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Arun Jayaram, Analyst
passages.text: Arun Jayaram, Analyst: Olivier, I was wondering if you could comment on some of the trends you are seeing at ChampionX. On a year-over-year basis, obviously, the comparable quarter from last year is different, but it looks like revenues were up in the mid-teens and margins are now pushing into the mid-20s. I wanted to talk a little about some of the trends here. How is SLB's ability to scale that business internationally compared with when you bought it?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: As you have seen, we are very, very pleased with the performance of ChampionX. I think this is the result of the integration team's success in making this business very resilient, as well as very successful in innovation and customer centricity, which are attributes of ChampionX in North America. You have seen that the quarter was remarkable in terms of top-line growth and further margin expansion for the fourth consecutive quarter, based both on the success and growth of production chemicals and on artificial lift, in North America, with more potential internationally. Internationally, as we mentioned in our prepared remarks, it would have been even better without the Middle East situation, as we have the optionality to expand the ChampionX portfolio internationally, particularly in the Middle East and across several offshore basins. This is progressing, and I think it will certainly be an upside to the ChampionX group's trajectory in 2027, both internationally offshore and, as the conflict comes to an end, with a further catalyst for ChampionX's success. We are very pleased. I think it reflects our ability to integrate and leverage ChampionX's technology, our global footprint, and our customer engagements to make this a success. We are very pleased with the performance. Congratulations to all the ChampionX employees and to the integration team. The combination in our Production Systems portfolio is attractive to our customers. The

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: feedback we are receiving from customers, both in North America and abroad, is that they like the combination. They like the power of production recovery and the potential to unlock significant further recovery and production performance through both production chemicals and lift technology, including digital. We are very, very pleased with the performance so far.

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer: As to the margin level, Arun, you are right. ChampionX has now reached the mid-20s on EBITDA, which is clearly accretive to the overall company. This is despite inflation pressures, particularly on chemicals. The synergies, including in G&A, have been higher than we expected and have mostly offset inflationary pressure, to the point that margins continue to expand quarter after quarter. We are clearly going to achieve our initial synergy target of about $200 million after 18 months post-acquisition, which is basically the end of this year. We are not going to stop there, and we are quite happy with the margins these businesses are generating.

passages.heading: Arun Jayaram, Analyst
passages.text: Arun Jayaram, Analyst: Okay. For my follow-up, I was wondering if you could elaborate on OneSubsea visibility as we think about 2027. You announced the Exxon Rovuma LNG award in Mozambique. Do you see 2027 as a year with a lot of greenfield activity in terms of larger awards? Could you speak to the visibility you are seeing as we extend into this deepwater cycle?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Thank you, Arun. I will not restrict this to 2027. OneSubsea awards typically generate revenue over multiple years. Whatever is booked in 2025 and 2026 typically reaches out to 2027 to 2029. Directionally, I think the success we have had in recent months and the bookings we are anticipating mean that we believe we will surpass the $9 billion booking target we have set across the two years. I believe this should translate into visible revenue growth in 2027 and 2028 and beyond. We believe the technology portfolio we have, the deliverability of our capacity to the market, and the multiple allowances we have created with joint feasibility studies with customers to secure FIDs and participate in the best economics and best recovery solutions for the customer all combine to make this very attractive. This includes subsea processing technology, where we are uniquely positioned to unlock recovery solutions for mature basins. All in, we are quite confident in the outlook for subsea, which is aligned with the deepwater cycle that has started. We believe we will benefit from it, and OneSubsea will be a growth driver for the company going forward.

passages.heading: Arun Jayaram, Analyst
passages.text: Arun Jayaram, Analyst: Great. Thank you.

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer: Thank you, Arun.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Your next question comes from Sebastian Erskine with Rothschild and Co. Redburn. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Sebastian Erskine, Analyst
passages.text: Sebastian Erskine, Analyst: Good morning, Olivier and Stephane. Congratulations on a strong North America quarter, obviously with 7% sequential growth. Maybe you can talk about some of the building blocks of that performance. Much of it came from production-linked revenue, obviously the ChampionX side and artificial lift, rather than activity-linked work? What are your expectations for North America next year outside of Data Center Solutions in the core business?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: We are indeed very pleased with the sequential growth in North America. I think we beat the market sequentially and year on year. We believe the factors supporting this are a combination of our market position in North American land—not only ChampionX and our production recovery portfolio there, which combines production chemicals and artificial lift solutions, but also our drilling technology and digital portfolio, which now includes the S&P Energy business. I think all of these factors will continue to support our performance in North America, including Canada and the U.S. Conversely, North America offshore and some of the activity we have in Alaska or offshore in the Gulf of Mexico will also continue to support North American growth and performance, with digital exploration and contracts across drilling and reservoir that will continue to give us growth. Finally, as you know, Data Center Solutions will serve as a new leg of growth in North America, growing at the rate you have seen. It is very impressive. We are well on track to surpass $1 billion by the end of this year as a run rate, and we are still on track to surpass $2 billion in run rate for 2027. You combine all of this—our differentiated portfolio and technology in North American land, continued differentiation in North American offshore, including Alaska, Digital, and then the uptick and new growth vector from Data Center Solutions—and you get a North American market

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: that is poised to grow despite market conditions that would qualify as a low-growth environment going forward.

passages.heading: Sebastian Erskine, Analyst
passages.text: Sebastian Erskine, Analyst: I appreciate the color, Olivier. Turning to Data Center Solutions, I noticed in the release that you expanded into Asia this quarter. I am curious how large the opportunity outside the U.S. could become for your business. Also, how is the customer base broadening beyond your initial hyperscaler contacts?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: I think we have the potential to grow and replicate internationally the setup we have put in place in the Americas. Now, it is early days. I think we are leveraging our hyperscaler contract and delivering for end use—for data center construction or development in Asia at this point—and replicating to some extent the capability we have developed with our manufacturing hub in Louisiana. We are expanding it with some satellite manufacturing and integration capability that we have deployed in Asia, and then delivering to our end customer in the Asian market. We believe this will continue to happen. The potential we see, as you have heard from the Meta contract in Canada and as we develop further hyperscaler contracting in North America, will still be centered in the short term on North American growth. We continue to diversify our customer base, and I think we will be in a position next year to develop and deploy further and inform you about this. Multiple customer contracts are being deployed and logged in our backlog, and they will support us going forward. Additionally, the acquisition announcement we made on Kelvion will only add to this. The feedback we are getting from existing and prospective customers in this domain is that they like the combination of manufacturing, engineering, and technology capability with Kelvion's technology portfolio. That supports thermal management and heat management in the data center space. It is an

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: equation that is difficult to solve, with a lot of efficiency and upside available. We will bring a pool of technology and integration to play as a partner in this infrastructure buildout.

passages.heading: Sebastian Erskine, Analyst
passages.text: Sebastian Erskine, Analyst: Thank you very much, Olivier. I will turn the call back now. Thank you.

passages.heading: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer
passages.text: Stephane Biguet, Chief Financial Officer: Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Your next question comes from Neil Mehta with Goldman Sachs. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Neil Mehta, Analyst
passages.text: Neil Mehta, Analyst: Good morning, team, and thanks for taking our question. I would love to dig into the 2027 commentary a little more. Can you provide some color on the outlook from a regional perspective? And as you look across your global footprint, where are you seeing meaningful trends in customer spending?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: I would not go into detail on the guidance for 2027. We provided color on the directional trends. But I will reaffirm that we see the market giving us the opportunity to grow in every basin across every division in 2027. The combination of the portfolio we have, the contracts we have put in our backlog, and our differentiated technology portfolio gives us upside in each of the basins. Each basin has a combination of deepwater—for Latin America, North America, Europe and Africa, and Asia—and conventional and unconventional activity for the Middle East and Latin America. All of these basins also have a need and increased investment in production recovery. Directionally, I believe, as we commented earlier, exploration will be very visible in Africa and the Americas. Deepwater will be very visible in the Americas, including North and Latin America, Africa, and Asia. Unconventional activity will happen internationally in Argentina and the Middle East. Conventional activity, controlled development, or production recovery will occur in every basin. Again, we believe this provides a tailwind across the entire portfolio and all divisions, as we expect every basin to benefit.

passages.heading: Neil Mehta, Analyst
passages.text: Neil Mehta, Analyst: Thank you. I really appreciate that color. Maybe as a follow-up, can you talk a little about the Digital offering and some of the opportunity set there from a customer perspective?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Yes. We are very pleased with the progress we are making in Digital. As we commented earlier, digital operations, particularly, and data and AI are the two vectors of growth that we are most excited about. Additionally, I think digital exploration is about to benefit from a secular trend coming into the exploration market. These are the three vectors of growth that we see supporting our growth ambition for the next few years. Digital operations, as we commented before, relates to both drilling and production operations. It is a combination of platform applications and edge applications that allow us to provide automated solutions for our customers. We have been commenting on the success we are getting in drilling automation and drilling optimization. I think the same applies to production optimization. Digital operations will clearly continue to be a growth factor going forward. Adding to that, digital exploration is benefiting from a secular trend, or a new upcycle in exploration. Every new frontier basin benefits from digital exploration to derisk development and exploration campaigns. We are seeing increased interest from our customers in investing in data, reprocessing, and digital AI capability to improve imaging and the capability we can provide to derisk exploration and accelerate success. Finally, data and AI as a new vector of growth and a new disruptor for the industry: with our Lumi offering and our AI Teller offering, we

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: are seeing early adoption that I think indicates this has the potential to disrupt and become a new vector of growth for Digital in our company.

passages.heading: Neil Mehta, Analyst
passages.text: Neil Mehta, Analyst: Thank you very much for the color. We will turn it back. Thank you very much, Olivier.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Your next question comes from Marc Bianchi with TD Cowen. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Marc Bianchi, Analyst
passages.text: Marc Bianchi, Analyst: Hey. Thank you very much. Following up on Digital, I know you did not want to get into too many specifics on the drivers for 2027. Given the strong year that seems to be unfolding for that business, do you anticipate it can continue at double-digit growth in 2027, given all the exploration visibility that seems to be coming in?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Are you talking about digital exploration or Digital at large?

passages.heading: Marc Bianchi, Analyst
passages.text: Marc Bianchi, Analyst: Digital at large.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Yes. For Digital at large, our ambition is to continue to operate at double-digit growth or higher. I think we have the attributes to do so. As I said, the combination of the digital exploration cycle, which is favorable as we turn into 2027, and digital operations, which started last year or this year and continue to be on a high-growth trajectory, will support us. We continue to make progress, as you have seen in the number of automated feet drilled year to date. Production digital is where we see the most upside, in our opinion—the most attractive opportunity we have going forward. We believe this will play out in 2027 and beyond. Finally, as I said, AI as a disruptor will play a role and support growth going forward. I believe these three areas, in addition to our resilient platform portfolio—the exploration data, digital operations, and data and AI—should combine to provide the legs of growth we are looking for: double-digit growth again in 2027 and beyond.

passages.heading: Marc Bianchi, Analyst
passages.text: Marc Bianchi, Analyst: Yes, very good. Thank you, Olivier. The other question was on the data center business. With Kelvion, you increase your content opportunity. I am curious about your appetite for further M&A to continue to increase the content opportunity, or is it more likely that we will see you increase that on an organic basis?

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: We are very pleased with what we have managed to get as an acquisition, and I think we will concentrate on closing it. We will concentrate on fulfilling the ambition and strategic opportunity we have unlocked with this. This will give us an opportunity to increase our share of the wallet per gigawatt. We have a significant backlog with a large and increasing number of customers, including hyperscalers, which will give us an opportunity to put this to work and participate in optimizing thermal efficiency. That will increase our share of the wallet and our participation in this market, allowing us to provide not only fit-for-purpose, modular manufactured solutions, but also to integrate more and more engineered thermal and manufacturing solutions for the market. This is where we will focus in the foreseeable future. Then, depending on how the market develops, we will see what could come next. This is where we are putting our focus going forward.

passages.heading: Marc Bianchi, Analyst
passages.text: Marc Bianchi, Analyst: Very good. Thank you. I will turn it back.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Your last question will come from Derek Podhaizer with Piper Sandler. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Derek Podhaizer, Analyst
passages.text: Derek Podhaizer, Analyst: Hey. Good morning. I just wanted to ask about Production Systems.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Good morning.

passages.heading: Derek Podhaizer, Analyst
passages.text: Derek Podhaizer, Analyst: You guided Production Systems up, I think it was high single digits, for the fourth quarter. Throughout the call, you mentioned production chemicals, artificial lift, the geographic ties into the ChampionX acquisition, and completions. We have talked about Venezuela and OneSubsea, which provide a lot of visibility there. Maybe you could just talk through the different levers for fourth quarter specifically, seeing that high-single-digit outperformance, and how we should think about this directionally as we move into 2027? I know we will hear more in January, but just some early thoughts on these different lines within Production Systems, which are obviously gaining momentum.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Yes. We have pretty good performance in Production Systems. We are very pleased to see our strategy on production recovery taking shape, and I think that is reflected in Production Systems' backlog and potential going forward. The fourth quarter has an effect from year-end product sales, and it includes OneSubsea. As we come through every year, year-end product sales are a factor that shapes the sequential performance of Production Systems. It is no different this year; in a year that is indicative or characteristic of that cycle, this effect is magnified. Going forward in 2027, we will not comment directionally at this point. But, as I commented earlier, we anticipate every division will experience growth in 2027. This one will be led by the combination of the portfolio you mentioned: ChampionX, subsea, completions, and OneSubsea. This is clearly a portfolio that will benefit from deepwater and from the short- and long-cycle activity outlook. We believe we will participate fully and outperform going forward. Production Systems is resilient across short and long cycles and has a durable backlog, particularly with subsea, that will give us legs of growth in 2027 and beyond.

passages.heading: Derek Podhaizer, Analyst
passages.text: Derek Podhaizer, Analyst: Great. That is helpful. To wrap up, again addressing 2027, I know it assumes the Middle East stays flat from the second half of 2026. You are calling for market growth in the mid-single-digit range. Can you help us walk through or frame the magnitude of the upside in this market if we do see a Middle East recovery? I do not know if you want to talk through it country by country, but just help us understand where that mid-single-digit growth could ultimately go if we see some form of resolution and recovery.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: First, to clarify, we have been commenting on the market outlook that we see at this point, based on our early engagement with customers and also on their reflection of some third-party analysis on the 2027 outlook. The combination of North America and international, assuming flat Middle East activity, is set for mid-single-digit year-on-year growth. We believe we are set to visibly outperform this, and obviously a Middle East resolution would only be a catalyst for additional growth. I will stop short of giving you exact guidance on this. It will be an international-led upcycle going forward. But you have seen my earlier comments that we are very pleased with our market position and performance in North America. Again, we have multiple legs of growth ahead of us in this cycle. You should consider the Middle East, depending on the resolution of the conflict, as having the potential to come back, if not exceed, previous activity levels before the conflict. Some countries in the region will not only have to mobilize activity to restore production capacity, but will also continue to accelerate their capacity commitments, whether in unconventional gas, gas, or oil in the region. Going forward, this is only a catalyst. But in 2027, at this point, we expect international growth despite the Middle East, with the Middle East being an additional catalyst going forward.

passages.heading: Derek Podhaizer, Analyst
passages.text: Derek Podhaizer, Analyst: Very encouraging. Thank you, Olivier. I will turn it back.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: I will now turn the call over to Olivier Le Peuch for closing comments.

passages.heading: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer
passages.text: Olivier Le Peuch, Chief Executive Officer: Thank you, ladies and gentlemen. As we conclude today's call, I would like to leave you with the following reflections. First, our third quarter performance demonstrates that momentum is broadening across SLB. Each geography and core division grew sequentially, with a gradual recovery in the Middle East complemented by solid growth in North America and continued strength across the international offshore markets. Second, our core portfolio is benefiting from increasing activity across development and production. The strength and resilience of our expanded production portfolio, together with growth in Well Construction and Reservoir Performance, position us to participate as customers optimize existing assets and develop future activity. Third, the international outlook continues to strengthen. Long-cycle offshore projects are progressing, the foundation for renewed exploration is taking shape, and new opportunities are emerging across several markets. Combined with continued progress in Digital and accelerating momentum in Data Center Solutions—which will be further expanded through the acquisition of Kelvion—we are well positioned to capture a broader growth opportunity across both energy and industrial markets. These dynamics reinforce our confidence in delivering differentiated growth and outperformance as we move into 2027. With this, we will conclude today's call. Thank you all for joining.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for joining. You may now disconnect.

3 energy stocks we approach with caution

 

Energy businesses quietly power the physical things we depend on, from cars and homes to e-commerce infrastructure. But they are at the whim of volatile macroeconomic factors that sway capital spending, like interest rates and commodity prices. Wariness surrounding these influences has caused the industry to underperform the market as it was flat over the past six months while the S&P 500 climbed by 8.2%.

Investors should tread carefully as timing cyclical companies is a challenging task, and any misstep can have you catching a falling knife. On that note, here are three energy stocks we're steering clear of.

### SLB (SLB)

Market cap: $79.34 billion

What began in 1926 with two brothers logging the first electrical measurements in a well, SLB (NYSE:SLB) provides technology and services to help oil and gas companies locate reservoirs, drill wells, and produce hydrocarbons.

**Why Are We Hesitant About SLB?**

1. Costly operations and weak unit economics result in an inferior gross margin of 21.2% that must be offset through higher production volumes

### Oceaneering (OII)

Market cap: $4.14 billion

Deploying a fleet of 250 tethered underwater robots around the globe, Oceaneering International (NYSE:OII) provides remotely operated underwater vehicles and subsea equipment for offshore energy exploration.

**Why Do We Avoid OII?**

1. Sales trends were unexciting over the last five years as its 9.8% annual growth was below the typical energy upstream and integrated energy company
2. Gross margin of 18.1% is below its competitors, leaving less money to invest in exploration and production
3. Low free cash flow margin of 5.3% for the last five years gives it little breathing room, constraining its ability to self-fund growth or return capital to shareholders

At $41.94 per share, Oceaneering trades at 17.9x forward P/E. ### ProPetro (PUMP)

Market cap: $953.4 million

Operating exclusively in the Permian Basin—one of America's most prolific oil-producing regions—ProPetro (NYSE:PUMP) provides hydraulic fracturing services that pump high-pressure fluid and sand into oil wells to release trapped hydrocarbons.

**Why Should You Sell PUMP?**

1. Annual revenue growth of 9.3% over the last five years was below our standards for the energy upstream and integrated energy sector
2. Costly operations and weak unit economics result in an inferior gross margin of 27.2% that must be offset through higher production volumes
3. Expenses have increased as a percentage of revenue over the last five years as its EBITDA margin fell by 7.2 percentage points

ProPetro is trading at $7.70 per share, or 29.2x forward P/E. Business outlook
With the volatility of the oil and natural gas markets, we expect customer spending to remain focused on capital
discipline, production optimization, and operational efficiency across both international and North America markets. At the
same time, efforts to restore production, rebuild inventories and strengthen energy security are expected to drive growth for
oilfield services.

years. We expect activity growth to be led by production services, drilling,

rket conditions
During the third quarter of 2026, oil and natural gas markets remained volatile due to geopolitical developments and
global economic uncertainty. These factors continued to disrupt global oil supply and contribute to supply constraints.
Oil prices decreased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2026. The West Texas Intermediate
(WTI) crude oil price averaged approximately $87 per barrel during the third quarter of 2026, compared to approximately $96
per barrel during the second quarter of 2026, or a 9% decrease. The Brent crude oil price averaged approximately $96 per barrel
during the third quarter of 2026, compared to approximately $103 per barrel during the second quarter, or a 7% decrease.
Higher commodity prices generally support customer activity and capital spending in the markets we serve, as operator
investment decisions are often influenced by expectations regarding future commodity prices.
Trade tensions and tariffs continue to influence the global demand outlook, with varying impacts across end markets.
We continue to monitor and evaluate the effects of these on goods imported into the United States, developments related to
trade policy and the potential effects of future tariff actions on our business, financial position, results of operations, and cash
flows.
Globally, we continue to be impacted by inflationary cost increases, primarily related to logistics, chemicals, and
cement, which we expect to persist for sometime.

Looking ahead, oil market fundamentals are likely to be supported by a supply-constrained market and the need to replenish depleted strategic inventories. Our business is exposed to a number of macro factors, which influence our outlook and expectations given the current macroeconomic uncertainty and continued volatile conditions in the industry. All of our outlook expectations are purely based on the market as we see it today and are subject to changing conditions in the industry.

•Chart outlook: We see continued strength in LNG and industrial gases, while viewing the space and data center industries as significant growth opportunities for our diverse portfolio.
