## SUMMARY

**Baker Hughes Company**(NASDAQ:BKR) reported third-quarter results highlighted by record backlog in its Industrial & Energy Technology segment and the strategic integration of Chart. Management reported total orders of $10.8 billion and updated its full-year 2026 earnings expectations to a midpoint of $5.27 billion in adjusted EBITDA. The company stated that structural demand for power generation to support AI infrastructure and the expansion of natural gas systems is driving a significant upward revision in its three-year order targets. Executives indicated that while near-term geopolitical conditions in the Middle East require a measured approach, the company remains focused on deleveraging its balance sheet and achieving long-term margin expansion through the deployment of the Baker Hughes business system across its newly expanded portfolio.

## INDUSTRY GLOSSARY

## Full Conference Call Transcript

**Operator:** Good day, and gentlemen. And welcome to the Baker Hughes Company Third Quarter Earnings Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. Later, we will conduct a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, press \*1 to raise your hand. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to introduce your host for today's conference, Mr. Chase Mulvehill, vice president of investor relations. Sir, you may begin.

**Chase Mulvehill:** Thank you. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Baker Hughes Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. Here with me are our Chairman and CEO, Lorenzo Simonelli; and our CFO, Ahmed Moghal. The earnings release we issued yesterday evening can be found on our investor website at bakerhughes.com. We will also use a presentation with our prepared remarks during this webcast which can be found on our website. As a reminder, we will provide forward looking statements during this conference call. These statements are not guarantees of future performance and involve a number of risks and assumptions. Please review our SEC filings and website for the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.

A reconciliation of adjusted EBITDA and certain GAAP to non GAAP measures can be found in our earnings release and presentation available on our investor website. With that, I will turn the call over to Lorenzo.

**Lorenzo Simonelli:** Thank you, Chase. Good morning, everyone. And thank you for joining us. First, I would like to provide a brief outline for today's call. I will begin with an overview of our third quarter performance. Including the continued strength in orders and then provide an update on our progress integrating Chart. I will then highlight key commercial awards that demonstrate the breadth of opportunities across our portfolio before providing a high level update on the macro environment. Prior to handing the call over to Ahmed, I will discuss our mature asset solutions, or MAS, offering.

This represents a growing opportunity that expands our role across the life cycle of producing assets, while helping customers optimize recovery, extend asset life, and maximize value. Ahmed will then review our financial performance. Provide fourth quarter guidance, and update our full year expectations. To close, I will highlight the progress we are making in shaping a new more industrialized Baker Hughes that connects capabilities to deliver integrated solutions across many end markets throughout the molecule to electron value chain. Let's turn to slide 4. We delivered another exceptional quarter. Reflecting disciplined execution, strong cash generation, and continued progress in our evolution into a higher value solutions led company.

The quarter also marked our first period reporting Chart following the close of the acquisition on July 16. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $1.42 billion with margins of 17.6% comparable to last year. We delivered strong performance across the portfolio, supported by a recovery in Middle East activity within OFSE, consistent backlog conversion in IAT, and early progress from Chase. Adjusted earnings per share were $0.70. Up modestly year over year as strong operational performance more than offset the impact of higher interest expense. Free cash flow remained strong at $769 million including approximately $200 million of integration restructuring, and closing related cash costs associated with the Chase acquisition. Turning to orders, demand remains strong across our key end markets.

Driving broad based strength within the portfolio. With the company achieving a book to bill ratio of 1.3 times. IET recorded $5.9 billion in of orders, representing a 1.7x book to bill ratio, including $1 billion of LNG equipment awards and $2.2 billion of power systems orders led by strong data center demand. This continued order momentum drove IET RPO to a new record of $39.4 billion, up 6% sequentially and 23% year over year. Further enhancing our visibility into future revenue growth. Supported by approximately $18 billion of IAT orders year to date and ongoing capacity expansions, we now expect full year orders of $21.5 billion to $23.5 billion.

Given the strength of demand and increased visibility into future opportunities, we now expect IET orders to exceed $50 billion over Horizon 2. The outlook reflects sustained investment across gas infrastructure, offshore production, data center, and industrial markets. Along with emerging opportunities in geothermal and space. Importantly, these equipment orders expand our installed base. Reinforcing the long term earnings potential from high margin aftermarket service upgrades, and digital solutions over the asset life cycle. Turning now to the recently closed Chase transaction. The acquisition represents a significant step in our strategy to broaden Baker Hughes exposure to attract energy and industrial growth markets. Chase adds complementary capabilities in thermal management, cryogenics, and carbon capture.

Enabling us to deliver more integrated solutions across the molecule to electron value chain. The combination also significantly expands our market opportunity positioning Baker Hughes with a total addressable market of more than $400 billion, with greater exposure to attractive growth markets including data centers, gas infrastructure, geothermal, space, and industrial gases. Turning to integration. We have made strong progress in the first 100 days. Already executing $70 million of our $325 million cost synergy target. We have established clear KPIs and accountability across the organization as we deploy the Baker Hughes business system and advance our people, systems, commercial, and operational priorities while maintaining business continuity. Ahmed will provide more details on cost synergies later in the call.

Importantly, the value creation opportunity extends well beyond cost synergies. Through the Baker Hughes business system, we see meaningful opportunities to improve Chart's manufacturing, sourcing, project execution, and commercial performance driving better delivery, higher productivity, and significant margin improvements. Together with the realization of synergies, these improvements give us confidence that Chase EBITDA margins can reach 22% to 23% by the second half of 2028, with further expansion beyond that. We are also moving quickly to capture the commercial synergy opportunities created by the combination. Our teams are working together across our highest priority accounts. With a regular cadence to identify and convert opportunities across the combined portfolio and installed base.

We are already seeing early proof points including a major power generation order secured by IET from a legacy Chart customer. This is a great example of commercial opportunities created by bringing these 2 companies together. With that, let's turn to key awards on slide 5. Q3 orders demonstrated broad based demand for our versatile portfolio across our end markets. With meaningful awards in data center, gas infrastructure, digital, nuclear, and energy-upstream markets. Starting with data centers, continue to expand our position in power generation for this rapidly growing market, securing 2 major awards in the United States. Year to date, we have now booked $4.9 billion of data center awards.

These wins reinforce the strategic importance of the market and demonstrate that Baker Hughes is increasingly a critical enabler of the power infrastructure required to support the rapid growth of AI. Reflecting the scale of the AI-driven power opportunity, we secured a major order to provide 1.1 GW of power generation capacity for a major US technology company. The project will support advanced computing infrastructure for model training, inference, and physical AI workloads. Additionally, we received a major power generation order from a US energy company representing approximately 500 MW of capacity for AI infrastructure development. In gas infrastructure, we delivered another strong quarter, with awards spanning LNG liquefaction and feed gas transportation.

Along with the strategic agreement in behind the meter power generation. We expanded our relationship with Venture Global through a major LNG award for the Plaquemines expansion, including IET equipment across 4 liquefaction blocks that utilize Chart cold boxes. This is an early example of the broader value we can deliver by combining the complementary technologies of Baker Hughes including Chase. We also secured a substantial order for Venture Global's Cloud Connector Pipeline project. Our scope includes an integrated compression solution using Frame 52E's gas turbines to support 1 of the largest LNG feed gas transportation projects in the United States. Beyond these awards, we strengthened our long-term with Venture Global through a new power framework agreement with GE Vernova.

The agreement covers up to 16 behind the meter power islands. Representing up to 10 GW of generation capacity and establishes a repeatable model to support Venture Global's LNG growth and potential adjacent data center development. Together, these awards further strengthen our long-standing relationship with Venture Global while highlighting the breadth of our leading LNG franchise across both liquefaction and pipeline infrastructure. We also continue to see strong demand for gas processing and offshore production infrastructure. We were awarded a substantial, integrated FPSO equipment package for a large offshore development. The award includes LM2.5 thousand aeroderivative gas turbines driving both power generation and gas compression equipment.

Highlighting the versatility of our turbine portfolio and our ability to support critical offshore infrastructure. Beyond new equipment, we continue to grow our life cycle services business. We secured a significant long term service agreement with SBM Offshore. Covering 27 LM2.5 thousand gas turbines across 4 FPSOs. Agreement combines maintenance and repair service with iCenter digital service for remote monitoring and diagnostics, enhancing equipment reliability and availability across these critical offshore assets. We also received several compressor upgrade awards in the Middle East and Asia. These awards reflect continued investment in our installed base and demonstrate the value customers place on enhancing the reliability, efficiency, and performance of existing assets.

While creating additional high margin, recurring aftermarket opportunities for Baker Hughes. Turning to digital. Industrial Solutions secured key Cordant and wind across data center LNG, and industrial markets. Reflecting continued share gains across balance of plant applications including third party equipment. These awards included a preferred supplier agreement, as well as sensing, protection, and asset health solutions supporting key customers. These wins demonstrate Cordant's expanding reach across both Baker Hughes and third party installed bases. In nuclear, we secured an order for and control valves across 6 reactor units in Europe. This award strengthens our position in the growing nuclear new build market, while expanding our installed base and creating attractive aftermarket opportunities over the life of these assets.

Turning to energy upstream. Our OFSE team secured several key awards across MAS and subsea, reinforcing the breadth of our capabilities and global customer relationships. In Pakistan, we signed a multiyear MAS contract with OGDC to optimize production and recovery across more than 120 wells in mature oil and gas fields. The program integrates our extensive subsurface expertise, surface production technologies, and digital solutions to help unlock additional value from existing assets while supporting greater domestic energy supply. In addition, BP awarded us a significant contract to provide integrated offshore production enhancement and stimulation services in the U.K. North Sea. Using our vessel based solution and StemForce technology, we will support new well development and enhanced recovery from mature fields.

In The Middle East, we continue to deepen our partnership with national oil companies leveraging our broad technology portfolio to help customers improve production performance and maximize the value of their assets. In Kuwait, KOC awarded Baker Hughes a significant multiyear contract to deploy fit for purpose production AI enabled solutions and hybrid Kymera drill bits. Also announced plans to establish an in country research and technology development center to accelerate innovation optimize upstream production, and build local expertise. In subsea, Eni North Ganal awarded us a substantial contract for Kuwaiti Northern Hub Development in Indonesia. Our scope includes deepwater horizontal tree systems, associated manifolds, subsea controls, and distribution systems, as well as Cordant digital solutions.

We also secured a significant integrated subsea system award from ENI for the deepwater Cronos gas development offshore Cyprus. Representing an important win for our subsea business in the Eastern Mediterranean. Finally, we recently signed 2 strategic agreements in Venezuela that bring together capabilities across resource development and energy infrastructure. Building on more than 60 years in the country, our installed base includes the largest artificial lift footprint significant flexible pipe infrastructure, and approximately 240 turbomachinery units across 23 sites. Positioning us well to support Venezuela's long term energy ambitions.

Collectively, these awards and strategic agreements demonstrate the breadth of the Baker Hughes portfolio, the growing value of our enterprise capabilities, and increasing demand for integrated solutions spanning molecules to electrons. Turning to the macro on slide 6. The macro environment continues to underscore the importance of energy security and reliable supply. Disruptions across key producing regions have tightened inventories and supported commodity prices. Reinforcing the need for continued investment global energy production and infrastructure. While the need for longer term investment remains clear, customers continue to take a disciplined approach to near term spending. Against that backdrop, we expect global upstream spending to be broadly flat year over year. With an improving outlook into 2027.

In LNG, we continue to see a favorable outlook with operators looking to accelerate projects where possible. With existing capacity and committed projects expected to bring global LNG capacity to approximately 800 MTPA by 2030. We see future FIDs supporting further growth to 950 MTPA by 2035 as countries increasingly prioritize supply diversity and reliable power generation. Demand also remains exceptionally strong across power markets. With AI adding another structural driver to global power demand which is expected to double by 2040. In The US alone, approximately 100 GW of incremental data center capacity is expected by 2035, requiring roughly 18 Bcf per day of incremental gas supply to meet the associated electricity demand.

The challenge is not simply generating enough power, but delivering reliable and scalable power where and when it is needed. As grid constraints persist, hyperscalers and industrial customers are increasingly looking to on-site and behind the meter power. This plays directly to Baker Hughes' strengths, across power generation and gas infrastructure. Positioning us to participate across the value chain as AI drives increasing demand for both electrons and molecules. Overall, the growing need for secure energy supply LNG capacity, and reliable power generation reinforces long term growth potential for our portfolio and our ability to deliver solutions that span from molecules to electrons. Now turning to slide 7.

I would like to spend a few minutes on mature asset solutions, an important part of our strategy to create a more resilient, higher value OFSE business. An increasing share of upstream investment is directed towards sustaining production and improving recovery from existing fields. For our customers, the opportunity is to recover more, produce reliably for longer, and ultimately manage the retirement or repurposing of these assets more effectively. For Baker Hughes, MAS creates a compelling opportunity to deliver outcome based solutions by bringing together capabilities from across our portfolio we can optimize value across the life cycle of mature assets. Our mass offering spans 3 core areas.

The first is recovery optimization, we help customers improve recovery factors and unlock additional resources from mature fields. We begin with a subsurface led assessment to identify opportunities and then develop an integrated solution around the specific needs and economics of the asset. This can increase economically recoverable reserves and extend the field life. The second is asset productivity and integrity. Where we help customers maintain and improve production while protecting the reliability of existing wells and infrastructure. By identifying performance constraints and applying the right interventions and technologies, we can restore productivity reduce downtime, and extend productive asset life. And the third is decommissioning and repurposing.

Where we help customers manage end of life liabilities efficiently while evaluating opportunities to create new value from existing wells and infrastructure. Our objective is to reduce the cost and risk of retirement while identifying opportunities to give existing infrastructure a second life. MAS can also support customers sustainability priorities by capturing and monetizing flared gas, or repurposing existing reservoirs and infrastructure for applications such as gas storage. This can unlock additional value while supporting lower emissions operations, and extending the useful life of existing infrastructure. What differentiates our MAS approach is our ability bring together capabilities from across Baker Hughes.

We lead with our strengths in subsurface, wells, and production, while drawing on IET technologies and selected partners where complementary capabilities are required. By early engagement and understanding the assets economics, we can develop integrated solutions around outcomes that matter most to the customer.
